page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor architecture (x86_64) running at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

In benchmark testing, the D64s_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core and image processing tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 10%. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance across both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read and write operations.

The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external Premium Storage, and accelerated graphics or hardware-based machine learning training are not natively supported. However, the inclusion of Intel AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference for small and medium models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated physical cores and large L3 cache provide high compute throughput per resource unit, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high parallel processing capacity without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware.

This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It is also appropriate for CPU-bound machine learning inference and general-purpose enterprise workloads that benefit from a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio.
